Potato Dumplings

Served at: St. Martin's Day (Martinstag)

Serves 4-6Prep 30 minCook 20 min

Potato dumplings, or Kartoffelklöße, are a traditional German dish commonly served on St. Martin's Day (Martinstag) as part of a festive meal honoring St. Martin. These dumplings are hearty and comforting, often accompanying roasted meats and red cabbage during the autumn celebration.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (900 g) starchy potatoes, peeled
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) potato starch or cornstarch
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • Butter or oil for serving (optional)

Method

  1. Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes, then drain and let cool slightly.
  2. Grate the warm potatoes finely or pass them through a potato ricer into a large bowl.
  3. Add the flour, potato starch, egg, salt, and nutmeg to the potatoes and mix gently to form a soft dough. Avoid overmixing to keep dumplings light.
  4. Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil.
  5. With wet hands, shape the dough into dumplings about the size of a golf ball.
  6. Carefully drop the dumplings into the boiling water. When they float to the surface, let them cook for an additional 5 minutes.
  7. Remove the dumplings with a slotted spoon and drain well.
  8. Serve warm, optionally with melted butter or as a side to roast goose or pork and red cabbage for St. Martin's Day.

Tips

  • Use starchy potatoes (like Russets) for the best texture.
  • If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour or potato starch.
  • For a variation, stuff dumplings with a small piece of crouton or cooked bacon before boiling.
